thread:
maria: Heads-up: during the least-privilege sweep I found ~28 principals with KMS:Decrypt via legacy role "admin-ops-v1". several look like vendor service accounts. need triage.

oleg: can you paste the query you ran?

maria: ```sql
SELECT principal, role, has_kms_decrypt
FROM access_snapshot
WHERE role = 'admin-ops-v1' AND has_kms_decrypt = true;
```

chen: ran a complementary check against kms_key_policies and found 3 keys with wildcard members. snippet: ```json
{"bindings": [{"role": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter","members": ["serviceAccount:legacy-agent@*", "allAuthenticatedUsers"]}]}```

anya: whoa `allAuthenticatedUsers`? that smells like a misapplied terraform module from onboarding.

devsec-bot: [automated] Policy drift alert PD-2026-221: KMS key policy contains wildcard members. Severity: high.

sam: immediate mitigation: quarantine affected keys, rotate, and apply narrower policies. follow KMS rotation runbook.

maria: also pause entitlement auto-removals for these principals until we confirm owners; otherwise we risk breaking prod.

oleg: owners for vendor SAs usually live in vendor-ops. pinging them.

chen: one principal shows decrypt events after hours. suspicious. can we pull full audit for that principal for last 90d?

maria: request submitted to telemetry: `GET /audits?kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*&principal=serviceAccount:vendor-app@`

devsec-bot: incident created INC-2026-190 "Legacy role grants exposing KMS keys to vendor principals" assigned eng-security. Priority: P2.

anya: proposed plan: 1) quarantine keys (rotate + disable old primary) 2) collect audit trail + owner evidence 3) notify vendor & schedule emergency rekey if unauthorized 4) patch infra onboarding module.

sam: i'll own step 1. will run rotation in canary then full. playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-key-rotation

chen: exporting decrypt logs to a locked project with 1y retention for the security review.

oleg: our entitlement-sweeper treats role deletion as removal; we need to update logic so KMS-affecting roles require explicit owner confirmation before revocation. opening issue now.

maria: add org-level gate: if role touches resources tagged `sensitive:kms` then bypass auto-removal and require manual attestation.

devsec-bot: [note] Compliance flag: wildcard KMS policies are a SOC2 finding until remediated.

vendor-ops: replied: we added the SA during onboarding in 2023 but cannot find PR evidence for the wildcard policy. opening an internal ticket to look for the change history.

sam: quick helper to list principals on a key: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy my-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=my-ring`

maria: prepare a JIT disable template for the SA if vendor can't produce owner proof: https://redwood.internal/templates/jit-disable

chen: forensic note: decrypts at 2026-05-10T23:41Z originated from an EC2 host in eu-west-1. correlating with network egress logs.

maria: schedule: canary rotation today 16:00 UTC, full audit by 20:00 UTC, vendor attestation due EOD tomorrow. if attestation fails we do JIT disable + rekey.

sam: starting canary, posting run id when ready.

devsec-bot: replay-archive job started RA-20260515-09 for audit export.

maria: i'll draft the incident summary and compliance note. keep updates here.

anya: also filing a terraform module patch to block `allAuthenticatedUsers` and wildcard SAs in onboarding.

oleg: filed ent-sweeper PR #842 to add a `sensitive:kms` bypass and require manual ownerproof.

maria: good work. leaving this thread as the single source for the incident. reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
